# Code Style and Quality Baseline

Applies to every TS/TSX file in the repo. Only a small subset of these conventions is
machine-enforced (the exact list is in reference `code-style-details`); the rest are review
conventions you MUST follow even though no linter will catch a violation.

## Size and Complexity (review conventions, not lint-enforced)

- Soft limit of 300 lines per file: one file, one primary exported concept. Past that, split by topic.
- Functions <= 50 lines; cyclomatic complexity <= 10; nesting <= 3 levels -- flatten with early
  returns and guard clauses.
- Parameters <= 4; beyond that use an options object. **Never use a positional boolean** as a
  behavior switch (`doThing(true)` is unreadable) -- use an options object or split into two functions.

Oxlint enforces `max-params` (warn at 4) and nothing else from this section. The other limits are
enforced by review only, so do not treat a green lint run as proof a file is within budget.

## Hard Bans (detail in reference)

- **No `any`** -- use `unknown` plus narrowing. Oxlint enforces this as an error.
- **No `enum`** -- use an `as const` object plus a union type.
- **Prefer `type` over `interface`**; the only accepted `interface` use is declaration merging.
- **Prefer named exports**; `default` only where a framework requires it.
- Comments explain **why**, never **what**. No bare TODOs.
- Prefer web standard APIs; Node APIs only under the explicit `nodejs_compat` cases.

Per-symbol naming conventions, the full type rules with the exact accepted `interface` exception,
module / barrel rules, comment rules, the `tsconfig.base.json` strict flags, the Workers runtime
constraints, and the table of which lint rules are actually machine-enforced (and which are inert)
live in reference `code-style-details`. Read it before naming something new, before adding a barrel
or a default export, and before assuming a green lint run proves anything.
